newsitem.title: UK: Dorling Kindersley off on CD-ROM concerns.
newsitem.headline: Dorling Kindersley off on CD-ROM concerns.

text.p: Industry-wide signs of serious weakness in the CD-ROM market pushed down the share price of Dorling Kindersley Holdings Plc on Friday, analysts said.
Dorling Kindersley's shares fell 19 pence to 485p, hovering just above a 52-week low of 480p set earlier in the day.

The drop followed negative comments on the CD-ROM market by three other small UK companies earlier this week. Multimedia Corp, Omnimedia Plc and MediaKey Plc each reported disappointing results and cited slower-than-expected CD-ROM sales.
"Dorling Kindersley is just about the best one out there ... but they can't avoid pricing pressures," said one analyst. "And they can't avoid being tarred with the same brush."
Another analyst noted the three CD-ROM companies reporting results this week were "...all saying the CD-ROM market is absolutely desperate, and they're not going to make any money".
The analyst said a lack of exciting products and access to free information on the Internet was holding back CD-ROM sales.
One analyst said he expects Dorling Kindersley's shares to fall about another 10 percent, while a second said he sees the shares dropping to about the 450p level.
